name: Liu Qingfeng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021-2026); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Liu Qingfeng is the founder,chairman and president of Iflytek, a supplier of voice recognition software.
Iflytek is headquartered in Heifei, the capital of China's Anhui Province.
Iflytek went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2008.

name: Simón Pedro Barceló Vadell
forbes_bio: Simón Pedro Barceló Vadell is the co-chair and largest shareholder of the Barceló Group, one of Spain's largest hotel operators and tourism companies.
The group traces its roots to Simon Barceló, who founded the business in 1931 as a transportation company and expanded to tourism in 1954.
In 1962, the company opened its first hotel on the island of Majorca, and through a series of acquisitions expanded overseas, starting with the Caribbean, then Costa Rica and later the U.S.
Today Barceló has more than 300 4-star and 5-star hotels with 65,000 rooms in 30 countries.
Barceló Vadell's cousin, Simón Barceló Tous, is co-chair but is expected to step down in 2025, when he turns 65 years of age.

name: Warren Chen
forbes_bio: Warren Chen is a cofounder of Chroma ATE, a supplier of automatic testing equipment for sectors such as automotive and semiconductors.
The company was set up in 1984 by Chen and other alumni of Taiwan's National Chiao Tung University, including Leo Huang who is also a billionaire.
Chroma's power testing equipment is finding increasing uses worldwide as the AI boom leads to rising electricity usage.
Chen struck out on his own and set up Dynacolor, a Taiwan-listed maker of video surveillance products, in 1991.

name: Chandubhai Virani
forbes_bio: Chandubhai Virani is the cofounder of Indian snacks maker Balaji Wafers, which sells a range of items including packaged snacks, noodles and confectionery.

Virani and his two brothers Bhikhabhai and Kanjibhai, who help him run the company, entered the three comma club after selling a minority stake to private equity giant General Atlantic in January 2026.
Before starting Balaji Wafers, the brothers were doing odd jobs at Astron Cinemas in the town of Rajkot in the western Indian state of Gujarat.
The name "Balaji" was inspired by a temple in their hometown.

name: Abigail Bennett
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Abigail Bennett's grandfather, Marvin Sands, founded a humble wine business in 1945 at age 21.
That small operation has mushroomed into a publicly-traded behemoth now called Constellation Brands, which generates nearly $10 billion in annual revenue.
The company is known for its relentless streak of acquisitions. Subsidiaries include Robert Mondavi wine and Svedka Vodka.
Constellation also holds the rights to Grupo Modelo's U.S. beer business, including its Modelo and Corona labels.
Bennett's uncles, Robert and Richard Sands, are former executives and current board members. Her brother, Zachary Stern, is also a billionaire.
The family received $1.5 billion (pre-tax) of cash to convert its enhanced voting shares to ordinary shares in 2022.

name: Fatma Tuba Yazici
forbes_bio: Fatma Tuba Yazici and her three sons became the largest shareholders in Diler Holding when her husband, Recep Sami Yazici, died suddenly in 2009.
She's CEO of Diler and Yazici Iron and Steel, among Turkey's largest iron and steel producers, and owns shares of publicly traded Asil Steel Company.
She lives in Beylerbeyi, one of the most beautiful areas of the Bosporus in Istanbul.
She's a member of the professional committee council for Iron Steel and Hot Mill Products Industry at the Istanbul Chamber of Commerce.
forbes_facts: Fatma Tuba Yazici is Turkey's only woman billionaire industrialist.
She doesn't grant interviews or provide photographs to the media, because she doesn't want to be recognized on the street.

name: Vladimir Melnikov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Vladimir Melnikov is the founder and owner of Moscow-based Gloria Jeans, one of Russia's largest fast fashion retailers.
Founded in 1988, the company later manufactured for Western brands such as Levi's and H&M.
The business expanded quickly in 2022 after Inditex, H&M and Uniqlo left the Russian market, allowing Gloria Jeans to rent out some of the vacated space.
Gloria Jeans operates more than 700 stores in Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan.
forbes_facts: In 2022 Melnikov gifted 1 million rubles to each employee who worked for Gloria Jeans for at least 10 years.

name: Ina Chan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2014-2021); Hurun Global (2014)
forbes_bio: Ina Chan is recognized as the third wife of the late casino kingpin Stanley Ho and mother to three of his children, Florinda, Laurinda and Orlando.
Born in Macau, Chan owns stakes in casino operator SJM and STDM, Ho's previous Macau investment vehicle.
She also has a stake in casino and hospitality company Macau Legend, where her daughter Laurinda Ho is a director.
Chan met Ho as a nurse hired to care of his first wife, Clementina Leitão, who was disabled following a car accident in 1971.

name: Yifeng Zhou
forbes_bio: Zhou Yifeng chairs Hongda Xingye Group, whose interests include industrial chemicals, coal and PVC packaging.
Zhou, a member of China's National People's Congress, this year called for more attention to be given to soil preservation in the country.

name: Xu Yi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022-2026); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021-2022); Hurun China (2018-2021); Hurun Global U40 (2021-2022); Hurun China U40 (2019-2021)
forbes_bio: Xu Yi  is the founder and president of Bilibili, one of China's largest media businesses.
Xu holds an associate degree from the Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications.
